diversity.imgAlt: Group of diverse and happy people.
diversity.desc: Diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) are three interconnected concepts that aim to ensure everyone has equal access to opportunities and feels valued, regardless of their individual characteristics.

education.title: Education and Social Awareness
education.imgAlt: Circle of diverse and happy people
education.desc: We promote awareness through the platform. We encourage understanding and respect for differences, combating prejudices and stereotypes. The IncluMove team embraces all users.

wellbeing.title: Well Being
wellbeing.imgAlt: Woman walking while having positive thoughts
wellbeing.desc: OMS defines well-being as a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease or infirmity. It is a holistic concept that encompasses various aspects of life, including physical health, mental health, emotional health, and social relationships.

mission.title: Our mission!
mission.desc: To democratize a technological solution that promotes access to physical, mental, and social well-being through an inclusive and welcoming platform. We want all bodies — with or without limitations — to be welcomed by our application and find in it a safe space for physical activities.

team.title: About us!
team.desc:
Our development team is made up of three third-year Systems Development students from ETEC Bento Quirino: Henrique Professor, Rodrigo Scatolin, and Samuel Augusto. Passionate about web development, we joined forces to complete the Hackteen challenge.

We thought a lot about the theme and decided to create an application that could help people with disabilities to exercise, since physical well-being is essential for everyone's mental and social health. Our goal is for IncluMove to be without limitations, so we dedicated a lot of time to ensuring the site's responsiveness and accessibility.

We had the support of our Web Programming teachers, classmates and relatives, who inspired us to create this project. At last, we thank everyone who helped us on this journey!

faq.faqSubheading: These are the most frequently asked questions by IncluMove users, if your question is not here, you can send us a message!

questions.question: Is IncluMove free?
questions.answer: IncluMove is a platform created to promote inclusive mobility solutions for people with disabilities, offering all services for free. There's no need to insert credit card information or any other payment method.

questions.question: Is there a way to contribute IncluMove's development?
questions.answer: By registering, you are already actively contributing to the project's development! You can also contribute by sharing your experiences, suggesting improvements, or pointing out any errors you find.

questions.question: I don't have any motor or neurological difficulties, can I use IncluMove?
questions.answer: Yes! IncluMove is an inclusive and welcoming platform designed to serve all users, regardless of their limitations. Even if you don't have motor or neurological difficulties, you can still benefit from the functions provided by our project and the community we are building.

questions.question: How do I contact to report a problem on the platform?
questions.answer: You can contact us through the contact form available on our website or by sending an email to our support team at <a href="mailto:inclumove@gmail.com" target="_blank" class="email-link" rel="noopener noreferrer">inclumove@gmail.com

questions.question: Is there a mobile app?
questions.answer: Currently, we do not have a mobile app available for download. However, our website is fully responsive and can be accessed on any device, including smartphones and tablets.

questions.question: I don't think I can finish my workout, what should I do?
questions.answer: If you're not feeling well or think you can't complete your workout, it's important to listen to your body. You can choose to end the workout early, take a break, or adjust the intensity of the exercise. Remember that the most important thing is to respect your limits and prioritize your health and well-being.
